_comment: Cross-language pricing contract. input/output are USD per million tokens. Both modelUsage.ts (MODEL_RATES) and pricing.rs (BUILTIN) must price every id here identically via longest-prefix match. Regression cases below caught a real Rust drift bug (dated Opus 4.0 + Claude 3 Opus mispriced). cacheMultiplierCases pins the OTHER half of costing: what a cache write costs, which is a multiple of the input rate chosen by the write's TTL. That multiplier was a hardcoded 1.25 in both engines until 2026-08-24 -- the 5-minute rate -- while workspacer's own sessions are almost entirely 1-hour, which bills at 2x.
THE BLOCK REGISTRY. Every array-of-objects block in this file must be declared
here and everything here must be a block — closure in both directions, so a new
block is a failure until someone says what its cases must carry, and a renamed
one cannot quietly stop being validated.
kind of validation existed for exactly ONE block of ONE fixture.

cases.why: USD per million tokens, priced by longest-prefix match in both tables.

cacheMultiplierCases.why: A turn's total USD, given the tokens it reports. Pins the cache-write TTL multipliers (1.25x at 5 minutes, 2x at 1 hour), the cache-read multiplier (0.1x), and the no-split fallback, identically in turnCostUSD (TS) and turn_cost_usd (Rust).

cases.note: GUARD: 4.10 must NOT be swallowed by the 4.1 legacy key (trailing-dash pin)
REGRESSION: dated Opus 4.0 id -> claude-opus-4-20 (Rust was pricing this 5/25)
REGRESSION: Claude 3 Opus -> claude-3-opus (Rust had no entry, fell to default)

cacheMultiplierCases.name: 5-minute write bills at 1.25x input
cacheMultiplierCases.note: opus input 5/M; the 5m TTL is the rate both engines used to hardcode

cacheMultiplierCases.name: 1-hour write bills at 2x input
cacheMultiplierCases.note: THE BUG: this priced at 6.25 while every 1-hour session was billed 10.0

cacheMultiplierCases.name: a turn holding both TTLs prices each portion at its own rate
cacheMultiplierCases.note: 400k at 6.25/M + 600k at 10/M -- no single blended multiplier gets this right

cacheMultiplierCases.name: writes with no TTL split fall back to the 1-hour rate
cacheMultiplierCases.note: no cache_creation block at all; the cheaper rate is the bug being fixed, so the documented fallback is the dearer one

cacheMultiplierCases.name: writes the TTL split does not account for fall back to the 1-hour rate
cache reads bill at 0.1x input
cacheMultiplierCases.note: reads are the cheap tier and the multiplier is unchanged by this work

cacheMultiplierCases.name: fresh input and output are untouched by the cache multipliers
1-hour write at the sonnet rate
cacheMultiplierCases.note: sonnet input 3/M -> 2x = 6/M; the multiplier rides the model's own rate
